text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- "Macedonia and Greece should continue talks within the U.N. framework. Several countries support Macedonia's candidacy for non-permanent member of the Security Council," Macedonian President Kiro Gligorov told a news conference in Skopje on Monday.

- New drug factory ICN-Macedonia to open at the beginning of 1997 with initial capital of 20 million German marks, of which 25 percent to be provided by Macedonian chemical industry OHIS and 75 percent by the U.S. company ICN-Costa Mesa of California.
- Macedonian children travelling to Albania required to provide a document showing they have been vaccinated against polio.
- Bulgarian foreign minister Giorgi Pirinski said Macedonia and Bulgaria will sign a declaration on strengthening of friendly relations.
- The head of the Greek liason office in Skopje Aleksandros Mallas received by Macedonian education minister Sofia Todorova. Cooperation in education to start between the two countries.
